text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on June 2 in history:
1420 - Henry V of England married Catherine of Valois, daughter of Charles VI, king of France.
1734 - In the War of the Polish Succession, Russia and Austria finally took Danzig after a siege which had begun the previous October.

1740 - Comte Donatien Alphonse Francois de Sade, known as the Marquis de Sade, French writer and man of letters, born. Best remembered for his sexual perversions, from which the term sadism is derived.
1774 - The Quartering Act was revived in Britain, forcingpeople in America to provide housing for British troops in America.
1780 - Riots began in London led by Lord George Gordon in protest against Parliament's plans to extend the Catholic Relief Act (1778) cancelling restrictions on Roman Catholics.
1793 - After three days of revolt in France, 31 Girondists were arrested and ousted from the Convention.
1840 - Thomas Hardy, British writer, born; best known for his novels "Tess of the D'Urbervilles" and "Jude the Obscure".
1857 - Sir Edward Elgar, English composer, born. Among his best known compositions are the "Enigma Variations" and his oratorio "The Dream of Gerontius".
1882 - Giuseppe Garibaldi, Italian leader and patriot, died. He became a central figure in the fight for the indepedence of Italy leading his guerrilla army in the capture of Naples (1860).
1896 - Broadcasting by electromagnetic waves was first patented on this day by Guglielmo Marconi.
1899 - Spain ceded the Carolinas, Pelews, Marianne and Ladrones to Germany.
1904 - Johnny Weissmuller, U.S. and Olympic swimming champion, born. He later turned to acting playing Tarzan in films from 1932-48.
1932 - Major Frank Holmes, a New Zealand engineer, struck oil for the first time in Bahrain.
1940 - Constantine, former king of Greece, born. He was the son of Paul I and succeeded as King in 1964. After he left Greece in a coup in 1967, the military regime abolished the monarchy in 1973.
1953 - The coronation of Elizabeth II took place at Westminster Abbey in London. This coronation was the first to be televised.

1961 - George S. Kaufman, U.S. playwright and twice Pulitzer Prize winner, died. Best known for his contribution to "Dinner at Eight" and "The Man who came to Dinner" and the Marx Brothers film "A Night at the Opera".
1979 - Pope John Paul II arrived in Poland in the first visit by a Pope to a communist country.

1987 - Andres Segovia, Spanish classical guitarist, died. He established the guitar as a serious classical instrument by his numerous concerts and by his transcriptions of many pieces of Bach and Handel.
1988 - In Canberra, the High Court unanimously rejected Britain's bid to ban further publication in Australia of the "Spycatcher" memoirs of former secret agent Peter Wright.
1992 - Denmark's voters rejected the EC Maastricht Treaty by the slimmest of margins, stunning the European Community and their own overwhelmingly pro-Treaty leaders.
1993 - Challenger Melchior Ndadaye toppled military president Pierre Buyoya in Burundi's first free elections to give the majority Hutu tribe its first national leader.
1994 - 29 people, including top Northern Ireland undercover police fighting the IRA, were killed when their helicopter crashed on a remote Scottish headland.
